family.description: This entry represents the first region from the so-called delivery domain from Lymphostatin. Lymphostatin is a key virulence factor of enteropathogenic and enterohaemorrhagic Escherichia coli, playing roles in bacterial colonisation of the gut and in the inhibition of lymphocyte proliferation and proinflammatory responses [[cite:PUB00164033]]. Lymphostatin is composed of six distinct domains which enable complex interactions with host cells. These domains include two glycosyltransferase domains, one PaToxP-like protease domain, an ADP-ribosyltransferase domain, a vertex domain and a delivery domain [[cite:PUB00164033]]. The delvery domain is involved in the receptor binding and translocation. It is an evolutionary conserved translocation and delivery apparatus in LCT-like toxins [[cite:PUB00164033]]. The delivery domain shows some flexibility and can adopt different conformations.
family.name: Lymphostatin, delivery I domain
